Tail latency is about how long it takes for requests to be processed after the tail is completed. In a distributed system, if workers are separate, the tail might take longer if the data isn't processed quickly. Need to consider how the system handles delays in processing the tail.

Request migration is about moving requests between workers when the tail is done. This could affect throughput and resource usage. Role switching would be when the system changes the role of a worker (e.g., from decode to prefill) to optimize performance. That's a bit abstract, so maybe explain how the system manages tasks and responsibilities.

GPU utilization is crucial. If workers are separate, each might have their own GPUs. Need to mention how the system manages GPU resources and whether they use them optimally. Also, how this affects throughput and cost.

Throughput tradeoffs involve balancing the system's ability to process requests and the usage of resources. For example, more requests might mean more GPU usage, but also more latency. The system needs to find the optimal trade-off.
